title: Leveraging Generative AI Tools for Enhanced Lesson Planning in Initial Teacher Education at Post-Primary
venue: Irish Journal of Technology Enhanced Learning
extended_summary:
This paper explores whether generative AI tools such as ChatGPT can support lesson planning in initial teacher education, with a particular focus on post-primary settings. The author frames the problem as the substantial time and effort required to create lesson plans and schemes of work, especially for pre-service teachers, and asks whether generative AI can help produce usable teaching materials efficiently and ethically.

The approach is a short report and critical reflection based on prompting ChatGPT (via a free GPT-3.5 account) to generate a review on AI in lesson planning, a sample lesson plan for a secondary computer science lesson on data, and a scheme of work for 5th year Leaving Certificate Computer Science. No post-editing was done on the generated text. The paper documents both the strengths of the outputs—speed, basic structure, and potential usefulness as a starting point—and their weaknesses, including fake references, repetition, spelling inconsistencies, and limited contextual awareness.

The context is initial teacher education at Hibernia College in Ireland, specifically the Professional Master of Education for post-primary teaching. The paper concludes that generative AI can help teachers save time and generate draft materials, but human judgment remains essential for quality control, ethical use, and contextual adaptation. It argues that teacher education should include AI literacy and practical guidance so future teachers can use these tools responsibly.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI chatbot for text generation and instruction following, accessed here via chat.openai.com using GPT-3.5 architecture.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate a short report, a lesson plan on introducing computer science data, and a scheme of work for Leaving Certificate Computer Science in initial teacher education. The author also reflected on the generated outputs and the prompt process.

findings.finding_summary: This paper is a single-author short report and reflection on using ChatGPT for lesson planning, not an experimental evaluation. The author reports that the tool produced usable lesson-plan structures quickly (less than a minute per prompt; the whole process took under 20 minutes), but the outputs also contained fake references, reduced word count, repetition, spelling inconsistency, and some context-inappropriate content.
findings.measure: Author reflection on output quality, usefulness, and time taken to generate lesson-planning materials

quality_tier_rationale: This is a reflective short report with no controlled design, comparison group, or quantitative outcome evaluation. Evidence is anecdotal and based on one author’s use of the tool.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests practical usefulness for rapid lesson-plan drafting, but the impact is unclear because the outputs required editing and included errors. No measured learning or implementation effect sizes are reported.
